site.name: Atlantic Cable Mine & Headframe Complex
overview: The Atlantic Cable Mine is a historic silver-lead-zinc mine at the north end of Rico. Its headframe and shaft remain a visible industrial remnant of the Pioneer mining district.
timeline: 1878 — John Glasgow and others located the Atlantic Cable claim.
Before 1900 — The mine's principal shaft was sunk.
1940s — The Rico Argentine Mining Company pumped the shaft and produced zinc-lead-copper ore during World War II.
moreHistory: USGS district geology describes the Atlantic Cable as a shaft mine with levels at 45, 62, and 183 feet below the surface. The mine produced silver, lead, zinc, copper, and minor gold. The preserved headframe provides a defensible identification target; this record does not imply access to underground workings.
